newsitem.title: USA: Legato says Unix-NT mix leveling off.
newsitem.headline: Legato says Unix-NT mix leveling off.

text.p: Legato Systems Chief Operating Officer Kent Smith said the company has begun seeing the mix of its products for Windows NT and Unix leveling off at around a 50-50 ratio.

The maker of storage management products also said it expects to ship its new Global Enterprise Management for Storage (GEMS) products for large organizations by October, providing a fourth quarter financial boost.
"The network business continues to be strong," Smith said. He declined to discuss further details of the second quarter, which ends today.

The ratio of revenues from products sold on Microsoft Corp's Windows NT system to Unix systems is important because average selling prices for NT products are roughly 50 percent of average prices for Unix.

Legato was the first to market an NT-based storage management product. A year ago, Legato's NT products were less than 20 percent of sales, Smith said, a percentage which has risen to about 50 percent "for the past couple of quarters."

For more sophisticated installations, connecting NT and Unix systems for example, he said average selling prices are higher than for straight NT systems and this area may provide an increasing business opportunity.
Shares of Legato slid after the company reported first quarter results, as some analysts said a shallow shortfall in earnings signified weakness of the shift towards NT.

Smith said Legato's business model remains in place, with an operating margin target of 26 to 29 percent and aims for 87 to 89 percent gross margins, with research and development expenditure at 17-19 percent.

Legato has traditionally concentrated on products for computer networks, and the move into the so-called enterprise market for large organizations represents a new market opportunity for the company, he said.
The company may face some pressure on the sales and marketing side, targeted at 33-35 percent of revenues, as it builds up a force to sell its GEMS product, he said.
Eventually, the sales force may grow to mirror Legato's current sales force in numbers, with about 40 people in the United States and 20 overseas, he said -- but this would not occur this year.
Smith said as early as next year the company's sales abroad could exceed its U.S. sales. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
